MINUTES

  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  BUDGET STUDY SESSION

  JUNE 6, 2018

An adjourned meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 8:13 a.m. in the Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR PRO
TEM MITCHELL.

2.  ROLL CALL

  City Council Members Present:  Huff*, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman*
  Arrived at 8:20 p.m.

  City Council Members Absent:  None

  City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

  Others Present:  Mark Young, KNN Public Finance

3.  PUBLIC COMMENT

  NONE

4.  ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

A.  REVIEW OF PROPOSED FISCAL YEAR 2018-19 BUDGET

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the information and discuss the
  programs and services to allow staff to prepare the final budget for presentation and
  public hearing on June 26, 2018.

  City Manager Prichard introduced Mark Young to review a detailed analysis of the
  City’s capital needs, exceptional revenues and fund balances as they relate to the
  Council’s desire to pay down the City’s unfunded accrued pension liability (UAL.)

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL  1
MINUTES (BUDGET STUDY SESSION)
JUNE 6, 2017
   Mark Young, KNN Public Finance reviewed the City’s financial position through FY 20-
  21 including the fund balances and exceptional revenue; and discussed the options for
  paying down the CalPERS UAL and funding the various capital improvement projects,
  including the option for financing the capital improvement projects on a tax exempt
  basis. He further reviewed the various scenarios and the impact each would have on
  the City’s general fund balance and reserve funds. He commented that although there
  may be a compelling argument for financing the projects, doing so will have a negative
  impact on the City’s general fund balance and will imbed a high expense into general
  fund. He further recommended against imbedding a fixed expenditure of this size in
  the City’s limited budget and recommended that the City pay $500,000 per year
  towards the UAL from excess fund balance over the next three years, with
  reconsideration of the City’s position at each budget adoption process. He commented
  that this approach is consistent with the City’s reserve policy to use one time revenues
  for one time expenditures.

  Following brief discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to undertake a three
  year program to pay $500,000 per year toward the UAL and use the remaining
  exceptional funds to pay for capital improvement projects.

  City Manager Prichard commented that the Audit/Budget Committee reviewed this
  information previously and concurs with Mr. Young’s recommendation. He further
  noted that the draft budget was prepared to include this recommendation.

  City Manager Prichard reviewed the FY 18-19 Budget Message and responded to a few
  requests for clarification from COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ. Administrative Services
  Director Whitehead noted that the categories on the pie charts will be combined so
  that they are easier to read.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead reviewed the General Fund revenue
  summary (page 19) noting that revenue is stable; sales tax is increasing slightly; and
  the budget includes $100,000 in new revenue as a result of an expected six months of
  increased business license taxes assuming voters approve Measure A. He further
  noted that the stable revenue continues to increase.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN regarding the previous land fill
  regulation fees that no longer exist, Administrative Services Director commented that
  based on a review by MuniServices, that revenue will be replaced by property tax from
  new homes. Brief discussion ensued concerning the estimated property tax revenue.
  Administrative Services Director Whitehead further reviewed additional revenue
  sources including concessions, QUIMBY fees, Highway Users Tax, SB-1 funds and
  other miscellaneous funds.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested if sufficient funds exist in special revenue
  or other funds, the City may want to consider adding a bike lane on Palos Verdes
  Drive East between Palos Verdes Drive North and the City limit to the north. Assistant
  City Manager commented that this matter will be brought before the Traffic & Safety
  Committee and the City can pursue grant funds for such a project.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead reviewed the sources and uses of the
  various funds (Exhibit F – page 38-39.)

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL  2
MINUTES (BUDGET STUDY SESSION)
JUNE 6, 2018
   In response to COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ, regarding a discrepancy between
  numbers reflected in the pie chart (page 23) and the numbers in the expenditure
  summary (page 27), Administrative Services Director Whitehead noted that the
  numbers will be reviewed and corrected in the final budget document.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead reviewed General Fund Operating
  Expenditures (page 27-28) including the public works project and UAL payment; and
  the Special Revenue Fund Expenditures (page 29-30.) City Manager Prichard noted
  that the City Hall renovation project will likely not occur in FY17-18 and will be re-bid
  in FY18-19. Administrative Services Director further reviewed the Fund Balance Policy
  Analysis (page 43) and the appropriation limit (page 45.)

  Upon review of the budget detail pages, COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ commented that
  because MAYOR HUFF will be taking over Chair of the South Bay Cities Council of
  Governments (SBCCOG) she will support the membership in the organization for the
  coming year, but she is still generally uncomfortable with the amount paid to
  SBCCOG compared to other city organizations. Brief discussion ensued concerning
  association dues and the benefits received.

  Brief discussion ensued concerning the budget activity detail including election
  expenses, travel/meetings, patrol services including sobriety check points, storm
  water permit compliance and landscaping/irrigation. MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL
  suggested that the City pursue further options for optimizing water usage at the
  parks.

  Discussion ensued concerning the expenses related to the City Celebration and the
  function and purpose of the event. Following discussion it was the consensus of the
  COUNCIL that the City Celebration and the Remember the Music Festival be run as
  two completely separate events with no Park & Activities Commission or City
  involvement other than providing the venue through a Park Use Permit. It was further
  suggested that the two events not be held on the same day in the future.

  City Manager Prichard reviewed the reference pages at the end of the budget document
  which detail actual and estimated building permit revenue, fund balance trends and
  personnel cost trends.

  Extraordinary Planning Department Revenue

  Planning Director Wahba reviewed the extraordinary planning department revenue
  including restricted revenue, building permit revenue and QUIMBY fees. He further
  reviewed pending development projects noting that the application for the proposed hotel
  project has been withdrawn.

  In response to MAYOR HUFF regarding funds related to equestrian specific expenditures,
  Planning Director Wahba reviewed the projected revenue for equestrian purposes and
  how the QUIMBY funds have been spent. Following brief discussion, staff was directed
  to prepare an analysis/recap of how the QUIMBY funds have been spent.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL  3
MINUTES (BUDGET STUDY SESSION)
JUNE 6, 2018
   MSRC Local Partnership Program

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided an overview of the Mobile Source Air
  Pollution Reduction Review Committee’s (MSRC) Local Government Partnership Program
  which provides funding for cities within the SCAQMD that participate in the AB 2766
  Subvention Fund Program and reviewed the presentation included in the staff report.
  She reviewed several project options that would qualify for this program including two
  Smart Electric Vehicle Charging Stations; a zero emissions, light-duty vehicle; and a zero
  emission trolley for the commercial area.

  Discussion ensued concerning the project options with the COUNCIL concurring that the
  trolley system is not the best use of the funds at this time, given the cost and that other
  funding options may be available.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE COUNCIL DIRECT STAFF TO SUBMIT AN APPLICATION FOR THE
  MSRC LOCAL PARTNERSHIP PROGRAM FOR FUNDING TO BE USED FOR
  TWO DUAL-PORT SMART ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING STATIONS AND
  ONE ZERO EMISSIONS, LIGHT-DUTY VEHICLE.

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

  At 10:19 a.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the open session portion of the meeting and the
  COUNCIL recessed into closed session.

5.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS – Government Code § 54957.6; Agency
  Designated Representative: City Manager; Employee Organization: City of Rolling Hills
  Estates Employees’ Association

B.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION – Government Code § 54957; Title:
  City Manager (Annual Evaluation Process)

No reportable action was taken.

6.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 10:50 a.m. MAYOR HUFF formally adjourned the meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Clerk

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL  4
MINUTES (BUDGET STUDY SESSION)
JUNE 6, 2018
